title: #laterinlife
transcript: So I recently started a new podcast. And yes, I know there are a ton of podcast out there, but I do think that this one is different in many ways. And I say that because it's called later in life. And what I'm trying to do is honour and celebrate and give visibility around regular people who are doing extraordinary things later in life. And what I mean by extraordinary is they're discovering something new about themselves, they're evolving, they're transitioning, they're. They're taking on a challenge that they pushed aside for whatever reason and are either on the other side of it and. And enjoying the, the fruits of that, or they're in the midst of that transition and explaining what that's like. And I find both of those really fascinating to talk about. There are three episodes live right now. One of them features Community Theatre. Steve doing theatre again at 58. We know and love him. And he talks about what his journey has been like. I think he's getting close to opening night, so break a leg, Steve. I have a conversation with Eden Lane, who you might know on TikTok as well. She is a retired journalist who just started writing plays a year ago, and she has six plays that she's written. One of them has been submitted for recognition. Major recognition. The most recent episode is with my friend Greg, who I've known for 20 years, and he has been someone who's Always identified himself as a capable professional. But then a crisis hit him during the pandemic, and he had to reassess and take stock in his 50s. And in development, I have a conversation with a woman who's starting college in her 60s. A single mother who discovered that she was queer and fell in love, uh, in her late 40s. And, um, what that's like being a single mother. Uh, a friend that I've known since high school who has had many careers and many experiences, many lives. She owned her own bakery, and now she's a special education teacher and getting her masters in special education. And what that's been like, um, identifying new parts about herself later in life. And someone who started doing stand up in their 40s. These are all regular people. These aren't celebrities. These are. These are people I know or I'm getting to learn through this experience. And showcasing just the everyday ways that people are learning new things about themselves. Because we are amazing. We can do great things when we put our mind to it. I have to remind myself of this. And I think hearing these stories might help you as well. And it's not just for anyone who's older. It's for anyone who wants to try something new or has fear holding them back or needs a nudge. And, um, I hope. I hope you take a listen, and if you like what you hear, please give It a rating and a comment in Apple Podcast. It really helps for a new show to find its audience. Um, so yeah.
